title: Pack and unpack a tar archive through streams
summary: Write tens to hundreds of small in-memory text files into a tar byte stream, collect the archive, then stream it back through the package's tar reader and read every entry, with each package's streaming API.
notes: The files of in-memory-roundtrip, through packages that read and write tar only as streams, on one thread with one operation at a time: each operation packs the entries into a tar stream, collects it into one buffer, streams that buffer back through the package's reader and reads every entry's body, all awaited before the next operation starts. The figure is the package's tar work (headers, checksums, padding, parsing) plus its stream machinery (Node-style streams or web streams) and the promise and event-loop turns it needs; UTF-8 encoding and decoding of the texts and one concatenation of the archive are the same in every adapter. In memory only, no file system, no timer or sleep.
